task: Stop the License Check job from reporting an egress-blocked license-URL lookup as a stale THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md (#95)

events.summary: Scoped to the License Check job's verify step, a new check script plus its self-test under scripts/ci, and the Makefile license target that shares the generation path. The egress allowlist is deliberately unchanged: adding golang.org:80 (option A in #95) would make the http fallback succeed but would open plaintext egress and hide the transient https failure it papers over. Pre-populating the module cache (option B) does not apply because the lookup is a go-get meta fetch of the module path, not a module download. Option C plus a bounded retry is what ships

Read the two failed runs on PR #91. Run 33526102258 shows go-licenses logging 'Error discovering license URL: getting file URL in library golang.org/x/text ... doURL(ctx, client, GET, http://golang.org/x/text?go-get=1): dial tcp 142.251.40.113:80: connect: connection refused' and the generated row '| golang.org/x/text | v0.40.0 | BSD-3-Clause | [Unknown](Unknown) |' diffing against the committed cs.opensource.google URL, followed by the misleading stale error; the earlier run failed the same way on golang.org/x/sys. Traced in go-licenses v2.0.1's vendored pkgsite source: golang.org/x/* has no entry in the static pattern table, so source.ModuleInfo falls into moduleInfoDynamic → fetchMeta, which tries https://<module>?go-get=1 and on any error retries with http://, and report.go resolves every library's URL concurrently in an errgroup and downgrades a failure to a warning plus LicenseURL=Unknown. The committed file regenerated byte-identical locally with the network open, so it is not stale; which module fails is whichever goroutine's https attempt hiccups on that runner

scripts/ci/check-third-party-licenses.sh check|write wraps the go-licenses report call: a run whose stderr contains 'Error discovering license URL' or whose output contains '[Unknown](Unknown)' is a discovery failure, retried up to GO_LICENSES_ATTEMPTS (3) with GO_LICENSES_RETRY_DELAY between attempts, and if every attempt fails the script exits 2 with an error that names the network/egress cause and says not to run make license. Only a clean run reaches the diff, so only a clean run can be called stale (exit 1, wording unchanged); an unrelated go-licenses failure propagates its own exit code. write mode replaces the file atomically and never writes on a discovery failure, so a blocked lookup can no longer put Unknown URLs into the committed inventory. The CI verify step calls the script and a self-test step runs first; make license uses write mode. The egress allowlist is unchanged

scripts/ci/test-check-third-party-licenses.sh drives the script against a fake go on PATH with no network: clean → 0; persistent discovery failure with 2 attempts → 2, message says 'not a stale' and never 'is stale'; fail twice then clean with 3 attempts → 0 with exactly two ::warning:: lines; genuinely stale → 1 with 'is stale'; unrelated go error → 3; write on clean rewrites identically; write on discovery failure leaves the file untouched. 11 assertions passed, written before the script existed and failing until it did. shellcheck reported nothing on either script
events.scope: the script's exit-code contract and retry behaviour under emulated go-licenses output; the fake go does not exercise go-licenses itself or the runner's egress policy

events.summary: With the network open locally, bash scripts/ci/check-third-party-licenses.sh check regenerated the inventory with zero 'Error discovering' lines and reported THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md up to date; make license in write mode left git diff --stat on the file empty; python3 scripts/ci/check-mutable-inputs.py passed for all three workflow files, so no action pin or mutable input changed
events.scope: the real go-licenses path and the workflow guard on a developer machine; the intermittent https failure itself is a runner-environment condition that could not be reproduced locally, so the retry's effect on it will only be observed on future CI runs

events.summary: A read-only review lane passed the change and raised one Important point: the final error blamed the network unconditionally, which is wrong guidance when a module's source URL is permanently unresolvable (moved repo, bad go.mod source). The message now names both possibilities and tells the reader to check the named module first; CI fails either way, so no outcome was ever masked. The lane's minor note that the fake go did not pin the report argv was also taken: it now rejects anything but './... --template hack/third-party-licenses.tmpl', so a drifted flag fails the self-test instead of only CI. Self-test and shellcheck re-run clean after both edits
events.scope: review coverage of the script, its self-test, the workflow step and the Makefile target by a lane that did not author them

events.summary: #95 is closed by option C plus a bounded retry within the scope stated in e1: an egress-blocked license-URL lookup now fails as what it is and can neither be mistaken for a stale inventory nor write Unknown URLs into it, at the evidence level stated in e4, e5 and e6

Complete at the self-test, local real-run, guard and review level; whether the retry absorbs the runner's transient https failures will only show on future CI runs, and the allowlist decision (no golang.org:80) is recorded in e1 for #26 to weigh when egress blocking is extended to release
